entities.summary: Azariah ben Moses dei Rossi was an Italian-Jewish physician, rabbi, and scholar. He was born at Mantua in c. 1511; and died in 1578. He was descended from an old Jewish family which, according to tradition, was brought by Titus from Jerusalem. He was known among Jews as Azariah min-Ha'adumim, a play on his name as well as a possible allusion to the fact that he lived in Catholic Italy, Rome being regarded as a spiritual heir of Esau. Combining an insatiable desire for learning with remarkable mental power, Dei Rossi early in life became exceptionally proficient in Hebrew, Latin, and Italian literature.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent rabbi and scholar in early modern Italy, Azariah dei Rossi played a crucial role in preserving Jewish knowledge and culture during a time of persecution. His works, including the 'Zohar Comentum', helped to establish a bridge between Jewish mysticism and Christian theology.
